question: How many different people flew to the Moon on Apollo missions (1968-72), including those who never landed on it?
source_title: List of Apollo astronauts (Wikipedia)
explainer: Twelve walked on the surface and twelve more stayed aboard the command module; three of them (Lovell, Young and Cernan) made the trip twice, on Apollo 8, 10, 11-17.

question: How many millimetres farther from Earth does the Moon drift each year?
source_title: Measuring the Moon's Distance (NASA Eclipse Web Site)
explainer: Lasers bounced off reflectors left by Apollo astronauts show the Moon receding about 3.8 cm a year, roughly the rate your fingernails grow.

question: How many minutes did Yuri Gagarin's 1961 spaceflight last, from launch to landing?
source_title: Vostok 1 (Wikipedia)
explainer: The first human spaceflight was a single orbit of Earth lasting about 108 minutes, shorter than most feature films.

question: How many Space Shuttle missions did NASA fly between 1981 and 2011?
source_title: List of Space Shuttle missions (Wikipedia)
explainer: Five orbiters flew 135 missions over 30 years, from STS-1 to STS-135, carrying 355 different people and logging more than 1,300 days in space.

question: How many Earth years does Neptune take to complete one orbit of the Sun?
source_title: Neptune (Wikipedia)
explainer: Neptune was discovered in 1846 and only completed its first observed orbit in 2011; a Neptunian year is 164.8 Earth years.

question: How many kilograms of Moon rock and soil did the six Apollo landings bring back to Earth in total?
source_title: Lunar Samples (NASA Astromaterials Acquisition and Curation Office)
explainer: About 382 kg in 2,196 individual samples, roughly the weight of a grand piano, most of it still stored at Johnson Space Center in Houston.

question: How many days did Valeri Polyakov spend in space on his record single flight aboard the Mir station (1994-95)?
source_title: Valeri Polyakov (Wikipedia)
explainer: The physician-cosmonaut stayed aloft 437 days and 18 hours, more than 14 months, a record that still stands; Frank Rubio's 371 days is the US record.

question: How many confirmed exoplanets were listed in the NASA Exoplanet Archive in September 2025?
source_title: The NASA Exoplanet Archive Hits 6,000 Planets (IPAC, Caltech)
explainer: The count passed 5,000 in March 2022 and 6,000 in September 2025, with more than 8,000 further candidates awaiting confirmation.

question: What was the launch mass of the James Webb Space Telescope in kilograms?
source_title: James Webb Space Telescope (Wikipedia)
explainer: Webb weighed about 6,200 kg at launch (6,161 kg by the detailed figure), roughly a bull African elephant, and about half of Hubble's 11,100 kg despite a mirror with six times the area.

question: How fast does the International Space Station travel in its orbit, in km/h?
source_title: Space Station Facts and Figures (NASA)
explainer: At about 17,500 mph (28,000 km/h, or 7.7 km every second) the station circles Earth every 90 minutes, so the crew sees 16 sunrises a day.

question: How many kilometres above the equator is a geostationary orbit?
source_title: Geostationary orbit (Wikipedia)
explainer: At 35,786 km a satellite's orbital period matches Earth's rotation, so it hangs over the same spot; that is nearly a tenth of the way to the Moon.

question: How many near-Earth asteroids had been discovered as of the end of 2025?
source_title: Discovery Statistics: Cumulative Totals (NASA JPL Center for Near-Earth Object Studies)
explainer: Around 40,000 near-Earth asteroids were catalogued by the end of 2025, with roughly 3,000 new ones found each year; fewer than 900 of them are larger than 1 km.

question: How many times more massive is the Sun than Earth?
source_title: Solar mass (Wikipedia)
explainer: The Sun holds 99.8% of the Solar System's mass; Earth would need to be duplicated about 333,000 times to match it.

question: What price per seat did Virgin Galactic set when it reopened spaceflight ticket sales in August 2021?
source_title: Virgin Galactic is selling tickets to space again, now for $450,000 per seat (Space.com)
explainer: The 2021 price of $450,000 bought a few minutes of weightlessness on a suborbital hop; earlier deposits had been taken at $200,000 to $250,000 a seat.

question: How fast was the Parker Solar Probe moving at its record closest approach to the Sun in December 2024, in km/h?
source_title: Closest approach to the Sun by a spacecraft (Guinness World Records)
explainer: On 24 December 2024 Parker passed 6.1 million km from the Sun at 192 km per second (430,000 mph), fast enough to cross the USA in about 20 seconds.

question: How many kilometres from Earth does the James Webb Space Telescope orbit, at the Sun-Earth L2 point?
source_title: Webb's Orbit at Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (NASA Science)
explainer: Webb sits about four times farther away than the Moon, far too distant for any repair mission, unlike Hubble in low Earth orbit.

question: What is the temperature at the core of the Sun in degrees Celsius?
source_title: Sun: Facts (NASA Science)
explainer: The core reaches about 15 million °C, hot enough to fuse hydrogen into helium, while the visible surface is a comparatively cool 5,500 °C.

question: What is the closest possible distance between Earth and Mars, in kilometres?
source_title: Go Outside and See Mars! (NASA Watch the Skies blog)
explainer: The theoretical minimum is 54.6 million km; the closest recorded approach was 55.7 million km in 2003, and at their farthest the planets are 400 million km apart.

question: How many kilometres does Earth travel in one full orbit around the Sun?
source_title: How big is Earth's orbit around the Sun? (Astronomy magazine)
explainer: With an orbital radius of about 150 million km, Earth covers roughly 940 million km a year, moving at around 107,000 km/h.

question: What is Pluto's average distance from the Sun in kilometres?
source_title: Pluto (Encyclopaedia Britannica)
explainer: Pluto orbits at about 39.5 times the Earth-Sun distance; sunlight takes around 5.5 hours to reach it, and New Horizons needed 9.5 years to get there.

question: What is NASA's estimated lifetime cost of the James Webb Space Telescope, in US dollars?
source_title: How much does the James Webb Space Telescope cost? (The Planetary Society)
explainer: NASA's share is about $9.7 billion over 24 years, including five years of operations, roughly double the early estimates; ESA and Canada added around another $1 billion.

question: How many kilometres from Earth was Voyager 1 in mid-2025?
source_title: Voyager 1 is about to be one light-day from Earth (BBC Sky at Night Magazine)
explainer: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 passed 25 billion km (about 167 times the Earth-Sun distance) in 2025, so far that radio signals take nearly a full day to reach it.

question: What valuation did SpaceX's December 2024 share sale give the company, in US dollars?
source_title: SpaceX valuation surges to $350 billion as company buys back stock (CNBC via NBC New York)
explainer: The $350 billion secondary sale at $185 a share made SpaceX the world's most valuable private company, up from $210 billion just six months earlier.

question: How many kilometres away is Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to the Sun?
source_title: Proxima Centauri (Wikipedia)
explainer: At 4.25 light-years, about 40 trillion km, Proxima is 1,600 times farther than Voyager 1 has travelled in nearly 50 years.
